changes.before: A pooled screen tells its story twice, once in images and once in sequencing reads, and spaCR brings the two together at the end. On the image side, Mask and Measure turn your microscope fields into measured cells, and Annotate and Classify turn those cells into phenotype scores. On the sequencing side, Map Barcodes turns reads into guide counts. Regression joins the two by plate and well. Join wherever your results begin.
changes.after: A pooled screen produces two data sets: microscope images and sequencing reads. On the image side, Mask and Measure segment your microscope fields and measure each cell, and Annotate and Classify assign a phenotype score to each cell. On the sequencing side, Map Barcodes converts reads into guide counts. Regression joins the two by plate and well. Start at the module that reads the data you already have.
changes.evidence: "tells its story twice", "brings the two together", "Join wherever your results begin". Module roles per module_workflows modules/*/inputs,outputs.

changes.before: Everything starts with your microscope images. Open Mask from Home, choose the channels and a segmentation model, and check the preview before you run it. The small counts database Mask leaves behind is only a tally, not yet a feature table.
changes.after: The image analysis starts from your microscope images. Open Mask from Home, choose the channels and a segmentation model, and check the preview before you run it. Mask segments the objects in every field and saves each field as a merged array, the image channels stacked with their label masks. Those merged arrays are what Measure opens next. changes.before: Sequencing is how a pooled screen learns which guide sits in which well or cell, and spaCR reads it two ways. Reads from a sequencer go into Map Barcodes. Around that core sit the planning tools, Experiment Design and Power, for before you acquire, and Dose–Response and Run Compare for your results.
changes.after: In a pooled screen, sequencing identifies which guide is present in each well or cell, and spaCR reads barcodes in two ways. Map Barcodes reads the output of a sequencer. OPS, which is part of Mask, decodes barcodes imaged cycle by cycle. In both cases, Regression joins the barcode identities to your phenotypes. This lesson also covers Experiment Design and Power / Design, used before acquisition, and Dose–Response and Run Compare, used on results.
